title: WR-90 cavity 22.86 × 10.16 × 30 mm filled with μr = 2.25, tan δm = 1e-3: TE101 resonance and its magnetic Q
source: A cavity filled with one material of μ = μr(1 − j tan δm): every eigenvalue k² is the lossless cavity's divided by 1 − j tan δm, so ω = ω0 (1 − j tan δm)^{−1/2}, Q = Re ω / (2 Im ω) = 1/(2 tan(½ atan tan δm)) ≈ 1/tan δm, with ω0 of TE101 from f = c/(2√(εr μr)) √(1/a² + 1/d²) (D. M. Pozar, Microwave Engineering, 4th ed., Wiley 2012, §6.3 and §6.7); evaluated separately from EMCraft's code

quantities.reason: second-order elements of 3 mm: eigenvalues converge as h⁴ (as for the copper cavity)

quantities.reason: exact for the discrete problem too: K/(1 − j tan δm) x = k² M x scales every eigenvalue alike, so only the iteration's convergence (1e-11) and rounding remain
the walls are perfect and the permittivity lossless: Q = Q_m
